'''José Oswaldo Lezama Serrano''' (born 1956) is a [[Colombians|Colombian]] [[mathematician]] who researches [[abstract algebra]] and specializes in [[Noncommutative ring|noncommutative algebra]]. Lezama graduated from the [[Industrial University of Santander|UIS]] in 1978 with a B.Sc. in Mathematical Education and obtained a PhD in 1983 under the supervision of [[Zenon Ivanovich Borevich]] from the [[Saint Petersburg State University]].<ref name=genealogy>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=118463|title=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> Since 1985 Lezama was a full professor at the [[National University of Colombia]]; he retired in 2020.<ref name=unaldoc>{{Cite web|url=http://ciencias.bogota.unal.edu.co/departamentos/departamento-de-matematicas/docentes|title=Professors of the Department of Mathematics of the National University of Colombia in Bogotá|access-date=2020-08-02|archive-date=2020-09-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929111302/http://ciencias.bogota.unal.edu.co/departamentos/departamento-de-matematicas/docentes/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Lezama was born in [[Bucaramanga]], Colombia. He studied at the [[Industrial University of Santander]] obtaining in 1978 a B.Sc. in Mathematical Education with a [[Latin honors|Cum Laude mention]]. In 1976 Lezama received a scholarship to study in the [[Saint Petersburg State University]] as part of an agreement between the governments of [[Colombia]] and the [[USSR]].<ref name=cvlac>{{Cite web|url=http://scienti.colciencias.gov.co:8081/cvlac/visualizador/generarCurriculoCv.do?cod_rh=0000244090|title=Oswaldo Lezama's CvLAC|url-status=dead}}</ref> His Ph.D. supervisor was [[Zenon Ivanovich Borevich]] and the work was titled ″The Group of the Invertible Elements of a Semiperfect Ring″. He obtained the title in 1983.<ref name=genealogy/>

In 1984 he came back to Bucaramanga and started working as professor in the Industrial University of Santander. The next year he moved to Bogotá and since then has worked as full professor at the [[National University of Colombia]]. He held this position until 2020, year in which he retired. In 1993, Lezama received the TWAS Scholarship ([[The World Academy of Sciences|Third World Academy of Sciences]]) as visitant professor in [[Trieste]], Italy. That same year he also visited the [[University of Buenos Aires]] and the [[Instituto Argentino de Matemática]] under the financial support of [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council|CONICET]] and the second mentioned institute.<ref name=cvlac/>

== Career ==

Since his return to Colombia, Lezama has had a very active participation in the mathematical community, taking part in national and international events as attendant, speaker and organizer. Between 1986 and 1991 started a research seminar on [[Ring (mathematics)|rings]], [[Module (mathematics)|modules]] and [[Category (mathematics)|categories]]. As a result, in 1994 he published with the mathematician Gilma de Villamarín a book called ″Anillos Módulos y Categorías″. Until 2002 he also hosted a seminar in commutative algebra, called SAC (″Seminario de Álgebra Conmutativa″, in Spanish).<ref name=cvlac/><ref name=sac2>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/a/unal.edu.co/sac2/|title=SAC2's web page}}</ref>

With time his interest in noncommutative algebra grew until the mentioned seminar changed its name to SAC2 (″Seminario de Álgebra Constructiva″, in Spanish) and the research in such matter started. The first aboarded topics were noncommutative [[Gröbner basis]] and [[Homological algebra|homological properties]] of noncommutative rings. In 2011, with his doctoral student Claudia Gallego, published for the first time the concept of skew PBW extension, which with time became his main topic of research.<ref name=cvlac/><ref name=sac2/><ref name=springer/>

In 2017 Lezama received the National Award of the [[Colombian Mathematical Society]], being the most notorious recognition of the country in the area.<ref name=premio1>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Este bumangués es el mejor matemático del país |url= https://www.vanguardia.com/area-metropolitana/bucaramanga/este-bumangues-es-el-mejor-matematico-del-pais-BGVL411374|location=Bucaramanga, Colombia |date= 2017-10-02|access-date=2020-08-02 }}</ref><ref name=premio2>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Ganadores Premios de Matemáticas 2017|url=https://scm.org.co/ganadores-premios-de-matematicas-2017/|location=Bogotá, Colombia|date= 2017-06-08|access-date=2020-08-02 }}</ref> In 2018 he received public attention when he published in several media an opinion article about the candidature of [[Sergio Fajardo]] to the presidency of Colombia.<ref name=fajardo1>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=El reclamo de ganador del Premio Nacional de Matemática a Sergio Fajardo |url= https://www.elespectador.com/noticias/politica/el-reclamo-de-ganador-del-premio-nacional-de-matematica-a-sergio-fajardo/|location=Bogotá, Colombia |date= 2018-06-02|access-date=2020-08-02 }}</ref><ref name=fajardo2>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title= Llamado de atención a Fajardo del premio nacional de matemáticas|url= https://colombiaplural.com/llamado-de-atencion-del-premio-nacional-de-matematicas-a-fajardo/|location=Bogotá, Colombia |date= 2018-06-01|access-date=2020-08-02 }}</ref>

In 2020, coinciding with his year of retirement of the National University of Colombia, a book called ″Skew PBW Extensions″ was published in the editorial [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] summarizing the results obtained by Lezama and colleagues/students among the years.<ref name=springer>{{Cite book|title=Skew PBW Extensions|publisher=Springer|year=2020|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783030533779}}</ref> Another notorious written work of Lezama are the called ″Cuadernos de Álgebra″ consisting on ten monographies (in Spanish) covering the basic topics of undergraduate and graduate abstract algebra, including [[Galois theory]], [[algebraic geometry]] and [[homological algebra]].<ref name=cvlac/><ref name=sac2/>

==Selected writings==

*[https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08071 ''Zariski cancellation problem for non-domain noncommutative algebras''] (2017), with [[Yi Wang (mathematician)|Yi Wang]] and [[James Zhang (mathematician)|James Zhang]]
*[https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02056 ''Extended modules and Ore extensions''] (2015), with [[Vyacheslav Artamonov]] and William Fajardo
*[https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.6639 ''Some homological properties of skew PBW extensions''] (2013), with Armando Reyes
*[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Oswaldo_Lezama/publication/233052507_Grobner_Bases_for_Ideals_of_s-PBW_Extensions/links/53f27d1b0cf2bc0c40eaff2f/Groebner-Bases-for-Ideals-of-s-PBW-Extensions.pdf ''Gröbner bases for ideals of σ-PBW extensions''] (2011), with Claudia Gallego
*[https://sites.google.com/a/unal.edu.co/sac2/cuadernos-de-algebra ''Cuadernos de álgebra'']
